x: Joe Flower went next and Ayton, of Mitcham, cut into this lead, so that when Martin went off he had about 10 yards lead over Norman Gunn. It was here that experience told and although Martin ran a very plucky race, Gunn reduced his lead to a bare yard or so.

In fact he almost went too slow and gave the rest of us a few hearts attacks when Ayton, of Mitcham, got to his shoulder at the last bend. Tommy, however, with a quick glance round, immediately sprinted away from him, and we realised Tom had been gently pulling our legs.
Moody, of the Police, won the 880 Yards, with Len Marchant beating the present Police Champion, R. Ayton, to take second place.
Ayton, who is also a member of the Mitcham A.C. In the 440 Yards another Police Champion came to grief when Syd Jarlett came through in fine style to beat W.
